content: We benchmarked the Doc2Vec models by scoring how well the document vectors represent the semantic topic structure: (i) calculating centroids for the 15 externally hand-coded categories; (ii) selecting the 100 nearest reports for each centroid; (iii) counting the number of incident reports (out of 1500) correctly assigned to their centroid. The results in Table 1 show that training on the highly specific text in the NRLS records is an important ingredient in the successful vectorisation of the documents, as shown by the degraded performance for the Wikipedia model across a variety of training hyper-parameters. Our results also show that reducing the size of the corpus from 13 million to 1 million records did not affect the benchmarking dramatically. This robustness of the results to the size of the training corpus was confirmed further with the use of more detailed metrics, as discussed below in Section sec:comparisons.
